todo_line: - [ ] 004 Implement and test explicit custom-group-removal follow cleanup through public Messaging APIs, including manual and auto-follow sources, idempotent stale-safe remove/re-add ordering, unrelated-follow preservation, and unchanged system-group behaviour.

validation.evidence: 38 tests, 0 failures. Covers cleanup durability and replay, manual/root/reply sources, late first stream creation, remove/re-add races, projection lag, unrelated/shared access, exact retries, explicit handler-list consistency, all supported add/remove return shapes, and Everyone/Admin no-ops.

79 tests, 0 failures. Covers retained newer follows with durable older cutoffs, stale manual/root/reply rejection after ordinary unfollow, blank and duplicate reply rejection without follow facts/state, success-only sender follow policy, historic event replay, deterministic projections, access composition, and send behavior.

notes: Messaging now records each custom-group removal in an idempotent member-scoped event stream keyed separately from Membership person streams, with group-specific generation cutoffs that survive aggregate restart and protect conversations created after cleanup acknowledgement. ConversationUnfollowed records older cleanup IDs/cutoffs with follow_retained=true, so projection replay preserves a newer follow while an ordinary unfollow cannot erase the cutoff. New MessageSent facts request sender follow establishment from a strong Messaging policy only after message acceptance; historic facts retain their prior direct-follow semantics, while blank and duplicate replies emit no follow. Public sends wait for the policy's durable progress, and custom-group add/remove preserve default, strong, eventual, explicit-list, and every supported Commanded return mode. Initial TDD runs reproduced all three review gaps (6 failures); intermediate diagnostics exposed the need for a non-person stream identity and retained-follow projection semantics before the final focused suites passed.
